OperationRunner.execute.name: execute
OperationRunner.execute.src:
func (r *OperationRunner) execute(task operationTask) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	key := r.byID[task.operationID]
	op := r.records[key]
	if op == nil || isOperationTerminal(op.State) {
		r.mu.Unlock()
		task.cancel()
		return
	}
	if task.ctx.Err() != nil {
		snapshot := cloneOperation(op)
		op.State = OperationCancelled
		op.ErrorCode = "cancelled"
		op.ErrorMessage = "operation cancelled before execution"
		r.finishLocked(op)
		r.mu.Unlock()
		if task.onCancel != nil {
			task.onCancel(snapshot)
		}
		task.cancel()
		return
	}
	if err := task.authority.validate(*op); err != nil {
		snapshot := cloneOperation(op)
		op.State = OperationCancelled
		op.ErrorCode = "caller_revoked"
		op.ErrorMessage = "caller activation is no longer authorized"
		r.finishLocked(op)
		r.mu.Unlock()
		if task.onCancel != nil {
			task.onCancel(snapshot)
		}
		task.cancel()
		return
	}
	op.State = OperationRunning
	op.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()
	_ = r.saveLocked(op)
	snapshot := cloneOperation(op)
	r.mu.Unlock()

	monitorDone := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(monitorDone)
		r.monitorCaller(task, snapshot)
	}()
	result, err := task.apply(task.ctx, snapshot)
	r.mu.Lock()
	r.completeLocked(op, task, result, err)
	r.mu.Unlock()
	task.cancel()
	<-monitorDone
}

//nolint:funlen // Lifecycle outcomes are mapped together for consistent transport semantics.
func (r *OperationRunner) setOperationOutcome(op *Operation, task operationTask, err error) {
	var warning operationWarningError
	var cleanupErr *session.TemporaryTrustCleanupError
	switch {
	case errors.As(err, &warning):
		op.State = OperationSucceededWithWarning
		op.Warning = warning.message
	case errors.As(err, &cleanupErr):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = "trust_cleanup_failed"
		op.ErrorMessage = fmt.Sprintf(
			"startup failed and temporary workspace trust cleanup may be incomplete; fix CLI configuration and remove the exact path %q manually",
			cleanupErr.WorkingDir,
		)
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrPersistFailed):
		op.State = OperationSucceededWithWarning
		op.Warning = "activation started but session metadata was not saved"
		op.ErrorCode = "persistence_warning"
		op.ErrorMessage = "activation started; inspect the returned session and persistence status"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrConversationChoiceRequired):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeConversationRequired
		op.ErrorMessage = "choose a saved conversation or explicitly start a new one"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrConversationChoiceInvalid):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeConversationInvalid
		op.ErrorMessage = "conversation choice is invalid for this card and session"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrSessionNotFound):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeNotFound
		op.ErrorMessage = "session was not found in the linked dashboard"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrLifecycleConflict):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeLifecycleConflict
		op.ErrorMessage = "session state does not allow this lifecycle operation"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrWorkspaceUnavailable):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeWorkspaceUnavailable
		op.ErrorMessage = "saved session workspace is unavailable; restore it before retrying"
	case errors.Is(err, session.ErrManagerClosed):
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = codeShutdown
		op.ErrorMessage = "Kankuro is shutting down"
	case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
		op.State = OperationCancelled
		op.ErrorCode = codeCancelled
		op.ErrorMessage = "operation cancelled or deadline exceeded"
	case task.ctx.Err() != nil && err != nil:
		op.State = OperationCancelled
		op.ErrorCode = codeCancelled
		op.ErrorMessage = "operation cancelled or deadline exceeded"
	case err != nil:
		op.State = OperationFailed
		op.ErrorCode = "lifecycle_error"
		op.ErrorMessage = "operation failed; correct its preconditions or inspect the session state"
	default:
		if task.ctx.Err() != nil && op.CancellationRequested {
			op.State = OperationSucceededWithWarning
			op.Warning = "operation completed; cancellation arrived too late"
		} else {
			op.State = OperationSucceeded
		}
	}
}

func NewSessionList(callbacks SessionListCallbacks) *SessionList {
	delegate := list.NewDefaultDelegate()
	delegate.SetHeight(SessionDelegateHeight)
	delegate.Styles.NormalTitle = delegate.Styles.NormalTitle.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("#8E44AD"))
	delegate.Styles.NormalDesc = delegate.Styles.NormalDesc.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("240"))
	delegate.Styles.SelectedTitle = delegate.Styles.SelectedTitle.
		Foreground(lipgloss.Color("#16A085")).
		BorderForeground(lipgloss.Color("#8E44AD")).
		UnsetBackground()
	delegate.Styles.SelectedDesc = delegate.Styles.SelectedDesc.
		Foreground(lipgloss.Color("#16A085")).
		BorderForeground(lipgloss.Color("#8E44AD")).
		UnsetBackground()
	delegate.Styles.DimmedTitle = delegate.Styles.DimmedTitle.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("240"))
	delegate.Styles.DimmedDesc = delegate.Styles.DimmedDesc.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("240"))
	l := list.New([]list.Item{}, delegate, 0, 0)
	l.SetShowTitle(false)
	l.SetShowStatusBar(false)
	l.SetFilteringEnabled(false)
	l.SetShowHelp(false)
	return &SessionList{
		list: l, callbacks: callbacks, primaryColor: lipgloss.Color("#8E44AD"),
		highlightColor: lipgloss.Color("#16A085"), gray: lipgloss.Color("240"),
	}
}

terminal widths. So pills are added only while they fit, and whatever does
not fit - including anything past MaxPillsShown - is summarised in a

FileRepository.doc:
FileRepository stores all configuration state in YAML files under one directory.

mu serializes read-modify-write sequences (list, mutate in memory, write
back) across all domains. It guards logical consistency on top of the
crash/interleaving safety WriteAtomic already provides for a single write.
It is a plain Mutex, not an RWMutex: several public readers are called
internally by mutators that already hold the lock (e.g. ValidateCard reads
workspaces/skills/personas/mcps while Create/UpdateIDCard hold it), and
Go's locks are not reentrant, so every exported method that touches disk
takes mu itself and internal call sites use the unexported *Locked helpers
that assume the lock is already held.

FileRepository.Fingerprint.name: Fingerprint
FileRepository.Fingerprint.doc:
Fingerprint stats every registry file refreshConfig reads and returns a
mtime+size marker for each, keyed by filename. It never opens or parses a
file - just one [os.Stat] per registry, so a caller can decide whether a
refresh is worth doing without paying for the read+unmarshal+sort it might
skip.

Two Fingerprints comparing equal (see FileStamp) is a "probably unchanged"
signal, not a guarantee: mtime granularity is 1s on some filesystems, so a
write landing in the same second as the previous stat can be missed. That
residual is accepted - every in-app mutation already calls Fingerprint
itself and sets the resulting baseline directly (see
coordinator.refreshDataSeeded), so a same-second write there is reflected
immediately regardless of the stat; only out-of-band hand-edits actually
depend on a later tick's stat noticing the change, and picking those up a
tick late is fine.

A missing registry file (EnsureFiles only runs at startup, so a user can
hand-delete one while the app is running) records a stable zero FileStamp
rather than failing the whole call: an error here used to return a nil
stamps map, which never compares equal to anything, silently disabling
this optimization - every registry got re-read on every tick, for the rest
of the session, with no signal that it had happened. A zero stamp compares
equal to itself tick to tick and differs from a real stat the moment the
file reappears. Any other stat failure (e.g. a permissions error) is still
returned as a real error.

FileRepository.UpdateSkillSources.name: UpdateSkillSources
FileRepository.UpdateSkillSources.doc:
UpdateSkillSources reads the current skill sources, applies fn, persists
the result, and re-syncs the skill registry - all under one lock
acquisition. This closes the read-modify-write race a caller doing
ListSkillSources -> mutate -> SaveSkillSources across three separate lock
acquisitions is exposed to: two concurrent callers can each read the same
starting list and one save clobbers the other's.

If fn's mutated list itself fails to persist, that error is returned
as-is. If the write succeeds but the subsequent registry resync fails
(e.g. a newly added source directory does not exist), the error is
returned wrapped in *SyncFailedError so callers can tell "nothing was
saved" from "the source list saved but skills.yaml is now stale" and
still refresh the UI in the latter case.

FileRepository.UpdateWorkspaceSources.name: UpdateWorkspaceSources

persists the result (assigning IDs to any new entries), and re-syncs the
workspace registry - all under one lock acquisition. This closes the
read-modify-write race a caller doing ListWorkspaceSources -> mutate ->
SaveWorkspaceSources across two separate lock acquisitions is exposed to.

If the write itself fails, that error is returned as-is - nothing was
saved. If the write succeeds but the subsequent registry resync fails, the
error is returned wrapped in *SyncFailedError so callers can still refresh
the UI to show the saved source list while surfacing that the workspace
registry built from it is now stale.

GenericCLIDriver.Kill.name: Kill
GenericCLIDriver.Kill.doc:
Kill terminates the agent's whole process group and closes its PTY. It asks
politely first (SIGTERM, so an agent such as Claude Code can save its
state), then escalates to SIGKILL if anything in the group - the leader or a
descendant - is still alive killGrace after the SIGTERM. A process that has
already exited on its own is treated as a successful kill.

The signals go to the group (negative pid), not just the child: pty.Start
runs the child with Setsid, so it leads its own session and group, and the
tools and servers the agent started are in that group. Signalling only the
child would leave them to die from the SIGHUP the closing PTY sends, which
anything that ignores SIGHUP survives.

The escalation looks at the group, not only the leader: an agent that exits
on SIGTERM (the normal case) must not let a child that ignores SIGTERM and
SIGHUP escape just because the leader is gone. Signalling -pid after the
leader was reaped is safe: the kernel does not reuse a pid while it is still
in use as a process group ID, so for as long as the group has members, -pid
can only mean this same group. (In a container whose init does not reap
orphans, an exited child stays a zombie and keeps the group "alive"; Kill
then waits out the grace period before a harmless SIGKILL.)

Known limit: a descendant that calls setsid() or creates its own process
group (a daemonising tool, a job-control shell) is outside the group and
survives. Pdeathsig is no alternative: it fires when the spawning OS
*thread* exits, which in Go can happen at any time.

d.mu is not held while waiting: watchProcess needs it to record the exit
and close done, so waiting for done under it would deadlock.

WriteFileAtomic.name: WriteFileAtomic
WriteFileAtomic.sig: func WriteFileAtomic(path string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error
WriteFileAtomic.doc:
WriteFileAtomic writes data to path using temp-file + rename for crash
safety: a crash at any point leaves either the old file or the complete new
one under path, never a truncated one.

It writes to a uniquely named temp file in the same directory (so two
concurrent writers never share a temp file), fsyncs the data before the
rename so a crash cannot leave a truncated file visible under the real
name, and removes the temp file on any error path. The temp file is named
".<base>.<random>.tmp", so a leftover from a crash does not match a
"*.<ext>" glob of the real files.

The directory must already exist; creating it is the caller's job.

Manager.Shutdown.name: Shutdown
Manager.Shutdown.doc:
Shutdown terminates all managed sessions, waits for activations that were
already in flight to finish (each notices the shutdown at its final check,
kills the process it just spawned and removes a new session's tmp copy), and
stops the watchers. It returns only once no process it could still be
responsible for is running and no watcher can write to disk any more. It is
idempotent. It returns how many sessions were running or waiting when it
started.

An activation that passed its final check before closed was set is already
Running; Shutdown collects its live list in the same critical section that
sets closed, so it kills that session like any other.

Sessions are killed concurrently: each Kill may spend a grace period on a
graceful stop, and doing them one after another would multiply it by the
session count. Kill comes before the watchers are stopped, so each record is
persisted as Terminated by Kill itself; the watchers then exit on m.stop
without their redundant final persist. One consequence: a watcher no longer
records ExitCode after a Shutdown kill - for a killed process that is just
the signal, so nothing is lost.

Sessions already Terminated are left alone: their record is current, and
rewriting every historic record on each quit would be pure churn.

Run runs the tests of one package inside a private root directory and
returns the exit code for [os.Exit].

TMPDIR points into the root, so every t.TempDir() of the run lives there

the old view is stored under the new view's key. Instead, return a Cmd

	c.conversationReadRequest++

	c.lifecycleRequest++
	c.lifecycleExecuting = false
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	c.conversationCancel = cancel
	return conversationReadCommand(

		c.activeDashboard,
		c.viewGeneration,
		c.conversationEpoch,
		c.conversationReadRequest,

	delegate := list.NewDefaultDelegate()
	delegate.Styles.NormalTitle = delegate.Styles.NormalTitle.Foreground(styles.PrimaryColor)
	delegate.Styles.NormalDesc = delegate.Styles.NormalDesc.Foreground(styles.Gray)

	delegate.Styles.SelectedDesc = delegate.Styles.SelectedDesc.
		Foreground(styles.HighlightColor).BorderForeground(styles.PrimaryColor).UnsetBackground()
	delegate.Styles.DimmedTitle = delegate.Styles.DimmedTitle.Foreground(styles.Gray)
	delegate.Styles.DimmedDesc = delegate.Styles.DimmedDesc.Foreground(styles.Gray)
	l := list.New(nil, delegate, 0, 0)
	l.SetShowTitle(false)
	l.SetShowStatusBar(false)
	l.SetShowHelp(false)
	l.SetFilteringEnabled(false)
	l.DisableQuitKeybindings()
	v := &DashboardList{list: l, callbacks: callbacks, viewport: viewport.New()}
	v.inputs[0], v.inputs[1] = textinput.New(), textinput.New()
	v.inputs[0].Placeholder, v.inputs[1].Placeholder = "Name (required)", "Description"

		inputStyles.Cursor.Color = styles.HighlightColor

	}
	return v
}

func editorKeyIdentity(keyMsg tea.KeyPressMsg) string {
	identity := keyMsg.String()
	switch identity {
	case keyCtrlC, keyCtrlS, keyCtrlE, keyCtrlX, keyShiftTab:
		return identity
	}
	switch keyMsg.Code {
	case tea.KeyEsc:
		return "esc"
	case tea.KeyTab:
		return "tab"
	case tea.KeyUp:
		return "up"
	case tea.KeyDown:
		return "down"
	case tea.KeySpace:
		return "space"
	case tea.KeyEnter:
		return "enter"
	case tea.KeyDelete:
		return "delete"
	default:
		return identity
	}
}

CardEditor.handleSpace.src:
// handleSpace handles space key based on focus.
func (e *CardEditor) handleSpace() bool {
	switch e.focusIndex {
	case FocusWorkspace:
		e.workspacePicker.SetSelectedID(e.workspaceID)
		e.workspacePicker.Open()
		return true
	case FocusSubWorkspaces:
		e.workspacePicker.SetMultiple(true)
		e.workspacePicker.SetExcludedID(e.workspaceID)
		e.workspacePicker.SetSelectedIDs(e.subWorkspaceIDs)
		e.workspacePicker.Open()
		return true
	case FocusUseTmp:
		e.useTmpWorkspace = !e.useTmpWorkspace
		return true
	case FocusShared:
		if e.sharingEnabled {
			e.shared = !e.shared
		}
		return true
	case FocusDashboardControl:
		e.dashboardControl = !e.dashboardControl
		return true

	case FocusPuppet:
		e.puppetSelector.SetSelected(e.puppet)
		e.puppetSelector.Open()
		return true

	case FocusAgentsMD:
		e.agentsMDEditor.SetState(e.agentsMD)
		e.agentsMDEditor.Open()
		return true

	case FocusSkills:
		if _, ok := e.skillList.SelectedItem(); ok {
			e.skillList.ToggleSelected()
			e.skillEdited = true
		}
		return true

	case FocusPersonas:
		if !e.settings.ShowPersonas {
			return false
		}
		if _, ok := e.personaList.SelectedItem(); ok {
			e.personaList.ToggleSelected()
			e.personaEdited = true
		}
		return true

	case FocusMCPs:
		if !e.settings.ShowMCPs {
			return false
		}
		if _, ok := e.mcpList.SelectedItem(); ok {
			e.mcpList.ToggleSelected()
			e.mcpEdited = true
		}
		// Auto-select mcp-cli skill
		e.autoSelectMCPCLISkill()
		return true
	}

	return false
}

func (s *SettingsView) updateEdit(msg tea.Msg) (component.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	var cmd tea.Cmd
	oldIDE, oldTerminal := s.input.Value(), s.terminalInput.Value()
	switch s.focus {
	case settingsFocusIDECommand:
		s.input, cmd = s.input.Update(msg)
	case settingsFocusTerminalCommand:
		s.terminalInput, cmd = s.terminalInput.Update(msg)
	}

	s.ideEdited = s.ideEdited || s.input.Value() != oldIDE
	s.terminalEdited = s.terminalEdited || s.terminalInput.Value() != oldTerminal
	keyMsg, ok := msg.(tea.KeyPressMsg)
	if !ok {
		return s, cmd
	}

	if keyMsg.String() == keyCtrlC {
		return s, tea.Quit
	}

	if keyMsg.String() == keyShiftTab {
		s.focus = (s.focus - 1 + settingsFocusCount) % settingsFocusCount
		s.syncFocus()
		return s, nil
	}

	switch keyMsg.Code {
	case tea.KeyEsc:
		s.mode = SettingsModeDisplay
		s.readBlocked = false
		s.settings = s.baseline
		s.input.Blur()
		s.terminalInput.Blur()
		s.input.SetValue(s.settings.IDECommand)
		s.terminalInput.SetValue(s.settings.TerminalCommand)
		return s, nil
	case tea.KeyTab, tea.KeyDown:
		s.focus = (s.focus + 1) % settingsFocusCount
		s.syncFocus()
		return s, nil
	case tea.KeyUp:
		s.focus = (s.focus - 1 + settingsFocusCount) % settingsFocusCount
		s.syncFocus()
		return s, nil
	case tea.KeySpace:
		return s.handleEditSpace()
	case tea.KeyEnter:
		return s.handleEditEnter()
	}

	return s, cmd
}
